content: The test image shows a corn ear completely replaced by a massive dark black spore mass, with husks peeled back revealing the dark powdery interior. This strongly suggests a smut disease affecting the ear (pod). Top candidates: Head_Smut or Common_Smut.

The Head_Smut reference shows dark spore mass filling the ear (with husks peeled), matching the test image well. Both show the entire ear replaced by dark brown-black spore masses. The test image shows a more robust/fresh infection with masses of dark spores, and the shape of the affected ear (teardrop-like, no normal kernels visible) aligns with Head Smut description — entire ear replaced by teliospores, with husks peeled back revealing the spore mass.

This is distinct from Common_Smut, which typically forms discrete galls on various plant parts rather than replacing the entire ear structure.
